final_message:
I've built the Workload Distribution Tracker workbook and a short Word memo answering the three questions. I re-ran the build after my last fixes and re-read the status and flag tables against the stated rules; they're consistent.

**1. Departments:** none are at risk. All five are within 5 points of 100%: PMO 101.1%, IT 101.5%, Professional Education 98.3%, Research 101.6% and Communications 96.5%. Communications is the closest to the edge.

**2. Individuals:** five people are flagged.

| Status | Name | Allocation rate |
|---|---|---|
| Over 90% (burnout risk) | Trevor Shaw | 103.8% |
| Over 90% | Zach Foster | 95.0% |
| Over 90% | Isaac Turner | 91.2% |
| Over 90% | Will Smith | 91.2% |
| Under 60% | Priya Desai | 53.8% |

- All four over-allocated people are part-time staff in Research and IT.
- Priya Desai charged no project time in the week of March 24, which may be leave that wasn't recorded. Check that before acting on the result.
- Nadia Green (88.8%), Alice Kim (85.6%) and Dana Singh (85.0%) are close to the 90% line and worth watching.

**3. Projects:** 6 of 9 went over budget.

| Project | Over by |
|---|---|
| Website Redesign | 79 h (140% of budget) |
| IT Implementation | 57 h |
| Customer Onboarding Platform | 26 h |
| Annual Plan | 14 h |
| Planned Giving Campaign | 4 h |
| Adult Outpatient Pavilion Construction | 1 h |

Across all projects, 2,488 hours were logged against 2,350 budgeted (105.9%).

**Assumptions and open items** (all recorded in the workbook's Assumptions & Exceptions tab):
- **Ellen Zhu** logged 155 hours but is not one of the 23 employees in the registry. I left those hours out of the department and individual results and kept them in the project totals. Customer Onboarding Platform is over budget only because of the 44 hours charged to it. HR should confirm who this is.
- **Monthly capacity** is 160 h full-time and 80 h part-time, because the export covers four weeks (March 3–28). If capacity is instead based on all 21 working days in March, Communications (91.9%) and Professional Education (93.7%) fall below the 95% target. March 31 is missing from the export, so Wrike Transition Initiative (98 of 100 h) could also end up over budget.
- **Individual rates** count project hours only, as a share of full capacity, so a normally loaded person sits around 85%. The workbook also shows a stricter view (project hours against the 85% left after admin time); on that basis 18 of 23 people exceed 90%.
- **Static figures:** the workbook holds calculated values, not live formulas. Re-run `scripts/build.py` to refresh it for a new month.
- **Input folders:** the `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders weren't there, so I used only the three reference files.

DONE

Files are in outputs/:
- Workload_Distribution_Tracker_March2025.xlsx (includes the Stakeholder Registry tab)
- Workload_Analysis_Responses_March2025.docx
